scene: 球场上，孩子们围成一圈报数，最后一个人喊出总数。The coach counted eleven players on the field.

senses.title: The cardinal number after ten
senses.definition: the number that comes after ten and before twelve
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在十之后、十二之前的数目
senses.example: She counted eleven chairs around the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她数了数桌边有十一把椅子。
senses.why: Old English endleofan meant one left, because eleven is ten with one left over; the name of the leftover became the name of the number itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 endleofan 的意思是「剩下一个」，因为十一就是十之后再余下一个；这个「剩下的一」最后成了数字本身的名字。

senses.title: A team of eleven players
senses.definition: a group of eleven people, especially a football or cricket side
senses.definitionCN: 由十一人组成的一队，尤指足球或板球队
senses.example: Their eleven won the match by one goal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的十一人队伍以一球之差赢下比赛。
senses.why: Because a full side in several sports has exactly eleven members, the bare number came to stand for the whole team.
senses.whyCN: 橄榄球、板球等运动的完整一队正好是十一人，于是光秃秃的数字直接代指整支队伍，数量变成了集体。

senses.title: Eleven o'clock
senses.definition: the hour one hour before noon or midnight, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 正午或午夜前一小时，日常口语中用来表示钟点
senses.example: We agreed to meet at eleven.
senses.exampleCN: 我们约好十一点见面。
senses.why: Clock time drops the word hour and keeps only the number, so the dial pointing at eleven becomes eleven o'clock.
senses.whyCN: 说时间时省略了 hour 一词，只留下表盘上的数字，所以表针指向十一就成了「十一点」。

intro.en: Eleven is an Old English numeral built from a phrase meaning one left, because it is ten plus one more.
intro.cn: eleven 是古英语数词，由意为「剩下一个」的短语构成，因为它是十再加一。

items.en: A form reconstructed as ain-lif is usually explained as one left over.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构为 ain-lif，意思是「剩下一个」。

items.en: The compound passed into Germanic as ainlif, still carrying the idea of one beyond ten.
items.cn: 这个复合词进入日耳曼语作 ainlif，仍带「十之外多一个」的意思。

items.en: It appears as endleofan, the form English inherited.
items.cn: 在古英语中写作 endleofan，是英语继承下来的形式。

items.en: Spelling shifted through elleven and enleven before settling.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写经过 elleven、enleven 等变化才逐渐固定。

items.en: Modern eleven keeps the number sense, while a team of eleven and eleven o'clock extend it.
items.cn: 现代英语保留数字本义，又用十一人队伍和十一点钟延伸出新的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same one-left-over numeral pattern; the near-meaning group places eleven among neighbouring quantities.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「十之后余一」的同一构词方式展开；近义组把十一放进相邻数量词中比较。

senses.title: The one after the tenth
senses.definition: the person or thing that comes after the tenth in a series
senses.definitionCN: 序列中排在第十之后的人或事物
senses.example: Her name appeared eleventh on the list.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名字出现在名单的第十一位。
senses.why: The ordinal ending -th marks a place in an ordered row, so the number eleven becomes the position after the first ten.
senses.whyCN: -th 词尾标记有序排列中的位置，于是「十一」被用来指前十位之后的那个位置。

senses.title: One of eleven equal parts
senses.definition: one of eleven equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体平均分成十一份后其中的一份
senses.example: He owns an eleventh of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他拥有这家公司的十一分之一。
senses.why: If a whole is cut into eleven equal slices, each slice is named by the ordinal, so eleventh also means one slice.
senses.whyCN: 把整体平均切成十一份，每一份都用序数来命名，所以 eleventh 也表示其中的一份。

senses.title: The last moment before a deadline
senses.definition: the final possible moment, especially in the phrase the eleventh hour
senses.definitionCN: 最后可能的时刻，尤用于 the eleventh hour 这一说法
senses.example: The deal was saved at the eleventh hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易在最后关头被救了回来。
senses.why: The day's eleventh hour is the last hour before noon, so the phrase grew to mean the final chance before a deadline.
senses.whyCN: 一天中的第十一个小时是正午前最后一个时段，于是这个说法引申为截止之前的最后机会。

definition_zh: 消除；排除；淘汰；清除
definition_en: to remove something completely; to defeat and remove from a competition; to rule out; to kill
core_image: 把碍事的东西一件件扫出门槛之外
scene: 清洁队把仓库角落的废弃物全部清走。The crew eliminated every trace of waste before the inspection.
sceneCN: 这里 eliminate 是「彻底清除」（第 01 个义项：把某物完全去掉）；句意是检查前工人清掉了所有废弃物痕迹。

pos.zh: 及物动词：消除；排除；淘汰；清除

senses.title: To remove something completely
senses.definition: to get rid of something completely, especially something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 把不想要的东西完全去掉
senses.example: The crew eliminated every trace of waste before the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 检查前工人清掉了所有废弃物的痕迹。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to turn something out of doors, with limen as the threshold, so the core picture is putting an unwanted thing outside the house.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义是「赶出门外」，limen 就是门槛，所以核心画面是把不想要的东西放到屋外。

senses.title: To knock a team out of a contest
senses.definition: to defeat a player or team so that they leave a competition
senses.definitionCN: 击败选手或队伍，使其离开比赛
senses.example: Our team was eliminated in the first round.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队在第一轮就被淘汰了。
senses.why: A losing side is pushed out of the tournament the way a thing is pushed out of the door, so the same verb describes sporting removal.
senses.whyCN: 输掉的一方被挤出赛事，就像东西被赶出门外，于是同一个动词也用来描述赛场上的出局。

senses.title: To rule something out
senses.definition: to show that something is not possible or not involved
senses.definitionCN: 证明某事不可能或与某事无关
senses.example: The police eliminated him as a suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 警方排除了他的嫌疑。
senses.why: When a suspect is cleared, that person is removed from the list of possibilities, which is again a mental clearing away.
senses.whyCN: 嫌疑人被洗清后，就从可能性名单里被拿掉了，这仍是一种思维上的清除。

senses.title: To kill, in formal use
senses.definition: to kill a person or animal, used in formal or euphemistic writing
senses.definitionCN: 杀死人或动物，用于正式或委婉的表达
senses.example: The disease eliminated entire herds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病消灭了整群牲畜。
senses.why: The strongest form of removal is to take a life, so the verb stretches from clearing objects to clearing living things.
senses.whyCN: 最彻底的清除是夺走生命，于是这个动词从清理物品延伸到清除活物。

intro.en: Eliminate comes from Latin eliminare, to turn out of doors, built on limen, a threshold.
intro.cn: eliminate 出自拉丁语 eliminare，意为「赶出门外」，其根是 limen（门槛）。

items.en: Limen meant threshold or doorway, the line between inside and outside.
items.cn: limen 意为门槛、门口，是内与外之间的界线。

items.en: The verb eliminare meant to turn someone out of the house.
items.cn: 动词 eliminare 意为把人赶出屋外。

items.en: Its participle eliminatus carried the sense of having been put out.
items.cn: 其分词 eliminatus 带有「已被赶出去」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb and widened it from people to things and ideas.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该动词，并把对象从人扩大到事物与观念。

items.en: Sports, medicine and logic each took the word for their own kind of removal.
items.cn: 体育、医学与逻辑各自取用这个词，表达本领域的「去除」。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the elimination family; the near-meaning group separates ordinary removal, total destruction and exclusion.
note.cn: 形近组留在 elimination 词族内部；近义组区分一般去除、彻底根除与排除在外。

entries.definition: To destroy something completely and root it out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「根除」，强调连根拔起。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something out on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「排除在外」，强调不让进入。

entries.definition: To beat an opponent, though not always removing them from a contest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击败」，但不一定把对方淘汰出赛。

normal.en: E- means out and limen means threshold: push it out the door.
normal.cn: e- 表示向外，limen 是门槛：把它推出门。

normal.en: A filter eliminates dust by keeping it out.
normal.cn: 过滤器把灰尘挡在外面，就等于消除了灰尘。

normal.en: A knockout round eliminates the losing side.
normal.cn: 淘汰赛把输的一方送出赛事。

normal.en: Detectives eliminate suspects one by one.
normal.cn: 侦探把嫌疑人一个个排除。

normal.en: Elimination is the noun built with -ion.
normal.cn: elimination 是加 -ion 构成的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a broom sweeping things over a threshold and out.
abstract.cn: 想象一把扫帚把东西扫过门槛、扫到外面。

abstract.en: Every sense is a list getting shorter.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都像一份名单在变短。

abstract.en: The word removes objects, rivals, doubts and lives.
abstract.cn: 这个词能移除物品、对手、疑虑，甚至生命。

examples.en: The police eliminated him as a suspect.
examples.cn: 警方排除了他的嫌疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个里面没内特」——里面没东西了，就是被清空、被消除

root: 拉丁语 eliminare，由 e-（出）加 limen（门槛）构成，字面为「赶出门外」；引申为清除、排除与淘汰。

sensesIntro.en: Eliminate starts with clearing an object out of the house, then clears a team from a contest, a person from suspicion and finally a life from the world.
sensesIntro.cn: eliminate 从把物品清出屋外开始，继而把队伍清出赛事、把某人清出嫌疑名单，最后把生命清出世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing an unwanted thing over the threshold and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把不想要的东西推过门槛、推到门外。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: waste and errors cleared away.
branches.cn: 物品线：废弃物与错误被清理掉。

branches.en: THE CONTEST: the losing side sent home.
branches.cn: 赛事线：输掉的一方被送回家。

branches.en: THE LIST: a suspect taken off the board.
branches.cn: 名单线：嫌疑人被从板上拿掉。

branches.en: THE LIFE: living things cleared from the world.
branches.cn: 生命线：活物被从世上清除。

branches.en: ONE PUSH: object, rival and doubt all leave the same door.
branches.cn: 同一推：物品、对手与疑虑走的是同一扇门。

intro.en: Eliminate is built from the prefix e-, the root limen and the verb ending -ate; its derivatives then add -ion, -or and -able.
intro.cn: eliminate 由前缀 e-、词根 limen 与动词词尾 -ate 构成；派生词再加上 -ion、-or 与 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin limen and eliminare are recorded; English added the familiar verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 limen 与 eliminare 均有记录；英语又加上了常见的动词词尾。

definition_zh: 别的；其他的；另外；否则
definition_en: other or different; in addition; otherwise
core_image: 手伸向另一个抽屉，那里放着不一样的东西
scene: 抽屉翻遍了也没找到，孩子又问起别的可能。She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
sceneCN: 这里 else 是「别的、其他的」（第 01 个义项：不同于已提到的事物）；句意是她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。

pos.zh: 副词：别的；另外；否则
形容词（后置）：其他的

derivatives.zh: 由 else 与 where 复合，义为「在别处」
由 else 加 -wise 构成，义为「以别的方式」（少见）

senses.title: Other than what was mentioned
senses.definition: different from the thing already mentioned, used after words such as something or anyone
senses.definitionCN: 不同于已经提到的事物，常用于 something、anyone 等词之后
senses.example: She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。
senses.why: Old English elles meant in another way, so else points away from the thing just named and toward a different one.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 elles 意为「以另一种方式」，所以 else 把注意力从刚提到的东西上移开，指向不一样的另一个。

senses.title: An additional person or thing
senses.definition: in addition to the people or things already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在已经提到的人或物之外再加一个
senses.example: Who else came to the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 还有谁来参加了会议？
senses.why: Asking who else means asking for one more name beyond the known list, so the different-thing sense also serves as an addition.
senses.whyCN: 问 who else 就是问已知名单之外再多一个名字，于是「不同的东西」这一层意思也用来表示追加。

senses.title: Otherwise, as a warning
senses.definition: used after or to introduce a bad result if something is not done
senses.definitionCN: 用在 or 之后或句首，引出若不照做就会发生的坏结果
senses.example: Hurry up, or else we will miss the train.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们会赶不上火车。
senses.why: The alternative way is presented as a threat, so else moves from another option to another, worse outcome.
senses.whyCN: 另一条路被摆成威胁，于是 else 从「另一个选项」滑向「另一个更糟的结果」。

intro.en: Else is an old Germanic adverb meaning in another way, related to the idea of other rather than to the modern word also.
intro.cn: else 是古老的日耳曼语副词，意为「以另一种方式」，与「其他」的观念相关，而不是来自现代的 also。

items.en: A root reconstructed as al- carried the sense of other.
items.cn: 可重构的 al- 词根带有「其他」的意思。

items.en: The adverb took the form alljas, still meaning otherwise.
items.cn: 这个副词作 alljas，仍表示「以另一种方式」。

items.en: It appears as elles in Old English texts.
items.cn: 在古英语文献中写作 elles。

items.en: Spelling settled toward els and then else.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写先固定为 els，再演变为 else。

items.en: The adverb was fixed after indefinite pronouns, giving something else and anyone else.
items.cn: 现代英语把它固定在不定代词之后，形成 something else 与 anyone else。

note.en: The look-alike group shows compounds and derivatives built on else; the near-meaning group compares other, otherwise and additional.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 else 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组则比较 other、otherwise 与「另外」。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「在别处、到别处」。

entries.definition: In another way, a rare synonym of otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以别的方式」，是 otherwise 的少见同义词。

entries.definition: A phrase introducing a warning or alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「否则」，用来引出警告或另一种选择。

entries.definition: A different person or thing from the one mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或代词，义为「其他的」，与 else 的核心义接近。

entries.definition: In different circumstances, or if not.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「否则、在其他情况下」。

entries.definition: One more, added to what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的」，对应 else 的追加义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat else as the pointer to another drawer, then let it add one more name or warn about a worse outcome.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 else 当成指向另一个抽屉的手指，再让它追加一个名字或警告更糟的结果。

normal.en: Else means the other one, not this one.
normal.cn: else 指的是另一个，而不是眼前这个。

normal.en: Something else is a different thing.
normal.cn: something else 就是别的东西。

normal.en: Who else asks for one more name.
normal.cn: who else 就是再问一个名字。

normal.en: Or else introduces the bad alternative.
normal.cn: or else 引出糟糕的另一种结果。

normal.en: Elsewhere puts the same idea in another place.
normal.cn: elsewhere 把同一个意思放到另一个地方。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing past the open drawer to the next one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手越过打开的抽屉，指向下一个。

abstract.en: The word always looks away from what is already known.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是把目光从已知的东西上移开。

abstract.en: One small word can add a name or threaten a loss.
abstract.cn: 一个短短的词，既能追加名字，也能威胁损失。

examples.en: She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
examples.cn: 她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。

examples.en: Who else came to the meeting?
examples.cn: 还有谁来参加了会议？

examples.en: Hurry up, or else we will miss the train.
examples.cn: 快点，否则我们会赶不上火车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔斯」——爱找别的，这个不行就换另一个

root: 古英语 elles，意为「以另一种方式、在别处」，源于日耳曼语 alljas，与 other 的「另一」观念同源。

sensesIntro.en: Else points to a different thing, then to one more thing, then to a worse alternative.
sensesIntro.cn: else 先指向不一样的东西，再指向再加一个，最后指向更糟的另一种结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing away from the known drawer toward another one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指从已知的抽屉移开，指向另一个。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENT ONE: not this, but another.
branches.cn: 不同线：不是这个，而是另一个。

branches.en: THE EXTRA ONE: one more name on the list.
branches.cn: 追加线：名单上再多一个名字。

branches.en: THE WARNING: the other outcome is worse.
branches.cn: 警告线：另一个结果是更糟的。

branches.en: OTHER AND MORE: a different item can also be an extra one.
branches.cn: 另与再：不同的东西也可以是在原有之外再添一个。

branches.en: CHOICE AND THREAT: the alternative becomes a consequence.
branches.cn: 选择与威胁：另一种选择变成了后果。

intro.en: Else is a free adverb that mostly combines with where and wise rather than taking a classical prefix.
intro.cn: else 是一个自由副词，主要与 where、wise 组合，而不是接古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin etymon, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语层，没有拉丁语词源，因此拉丁列表为空。

items.exampleCN: 它把 else 放在不定代词之后。

items.exampleCN: 它是最常见的搭配之一。

definition_zh: 在别处；到别处；在其他地方
definition_en: in or to another place; in other places generally
core_image: 目光越过眼前这块地方，落在远处的另一片区域
scene: 聚会散场后，主人把多余的椅子搬到别处。The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
sceneCN: 这里 elsewhere 是「到别处」（第 01 个义项：到另一个地方）；句意是聚会结束后多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

pos.zh: 副词：在别处；到别处；在其他地方

derivatives.zh: 复合成分，义为「别的」，与 where 合成 elsewhere
复合成分，义为「哪里」，与 else 合成 elsewhere

senses.title: In or to another place
senses.definition: in or to a different place from the one already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在或到一个不同于已提及地点的地方
senses.example: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。
senses.why: Else supplies the idea of another and where supplies place, so elsewhere is simply the place that is not here.
senses.whyCN: else 提供「另一个」的意思，where 提供「地方」，所以 elsewhere 就是那个不在这里的地方。

senses.title: In other places in general
senses.definition: in other places, considered as a group rather than one specific place
senses.definitionCN: 泛指其他多个地方，而不是某一个具体地点
senses.example: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
senses.exampleCN: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。
senses.why: The same compound can widen from one other place to any other place, so the word also serves as a general contrast.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合词可以从「另一个地方」扩大到「任何其他地方」，于是它也用来作总体对比。

senses.title: In another source or part of a text
senses.titleCN: 在别处（指其他来源或篇章）
senses.definition: in another part of a book, report or set of records
senses.definitionCN: 在同一本书、报告或记录的其他部分
senses.example: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
senses.exampleCN: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。
senses.why: A text is treated as a space with places, so a cross-reference sends the reader to a different spot in that space.
senses.whyCN: 文本被当成一个有地点可走的空间，于是交叉引用就是把读者送到这个空间里的另一处。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a transparent compound of else and where, already present in Old English.
intro.cn: elsewhere 是 else 与 where 的透明复合词，古英语中已经存在。

items.en: The compound appears as elleshwær, meaning in another place.
items.cn: 古英语作 elleshwær，意为「在另一个地方」。

items.en: Spelling passed through elleswhere and elsquer.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写经过 elleswhere、elsquer 等形式。

items.en: Printing helped fix the modern spelling elsewhere.
items.cn: 印刷术帮助固定了现代拼写 elsewhere。

items.en: The word extended from physical places to sources and parts of texts.
items.cn: 这个词从物理地点扩展到资料来源与文本部分。

items.en: It is now a standard adverb in news, law and academic writing.
items.cn: 如今它是新闻、法律与学术写作中的标准副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the else and where building blocks; the near-meaning group places elsewhere among other place words.
note.cn: 形近组展示 else 与 where 这两块构件；近义组把 elsewhere 放进其他地点词中比较。

entries.definition: The other element that supplies the idea of another.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「另一个」的意思。

entries.definition: The element that supplies place.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「地方」的意思。

entries.definition: In all places, built with the same place element.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带 -where 的地点词，义为「到处」。

entries.definition: In or to an unspecified place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在某处」，地点同样不确定。

entries.definition: In or to a foreign country.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在国外」，是 elsewhere 的一种具体化。

entries.definition: At a distance from the current place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「离开、在远处」，强调距离。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split elsewhere into else plus where, then move the reader from one room to another.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 elsewhere 拆成 else 加 where，再把读者从一个房间带到另一个房间。

normal.en: Else plus where means the other place.
normal.cn: else 加 where 就是「另一个地方」。

normal.en: If it is not here, look elsewhere.
normal.cn: 如果不在这里，就到别处找。

normal.en: Elsewhere in Europe marks a wider contrast.
normal.cn: elsewhere in Europe 表示更大范围的对比。

normal.en: A cross-reference sends you elsewhere in the book.
normal.cn: 交叉引用把你送到书里的别处。

normal.en: Everywhere and somewhere share the same -where.
normal.cn: everywhere 与 somewhere 都带同一个 -where。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight leaving this room and landing on another.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯离开这个房间，落到另一个房间。

abstract.en: The word is a small map with only two points: here and not here.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一张只有两个点的小地图：这里，和不在这里。

abstract.en: A footnote is elsewhere made visible.
abstract.cn: 脚注就是被标出来的「别处」。

examples.en: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
examples.cn: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

examples.en: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
examples.cn: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。

examples.en: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
examples.cn: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔斯维尔」——不是这儿，是别的哪儿

root: 由 else（别的）与 where（哪里）复合而成，古英语作 elleshwær，字面就是「在另一个地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Elsewhere begins as one other place, widens to other places in general, and then enters texts as another source.
sensesIntro.cn: elsewhere 从某一个别处开始，扩大到泛指其他地方，再进入文本表示另一个出处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze sliding past the present spot to a distant one.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光越过眼前的位置，滑向远处另一处。

branches.en: THE OTHER SPOT: a specific place that is not here.
branches.cn: 另一处：一个具体但不在这里的地点。

branches.en: THE WIDER WORLD: other places taken together.
branches.cn: 更广的世界：把其他地方合起来看。

branches.en: THE TEXT: another page or source.
branches.cn: 文本线：另一页或另一个来源。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: one other place can widen into many.
branches.cn: 一与多：一个别处可以扩大成许多别处。

branches.en: SPACE AND PAGE: a place word becomes a reading direction.
branches.cn: 空间与书页：地点词变成了阅读方向。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a compound of two free morphemes, else and where, with no classical prefix.
intro.cn: elsewhere 由 else 与 where 两个自由语素复合而成，没有古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic, so there is no Latin entry to list.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属于日耳曼语层，因此没有可列的拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 everywhere 与 somewhere 中。

definition_zh: 电子邮件；电子邮件系统；发电子邮件
definition_en: a message sent electronically over a network; the email system; to send such a message
core_image: 一封信化作光点，沿着看不见的线飞进对方的屏幕
scene: 地铁进站前，她低头用手机回完了最后一封信。She checked her email before the train arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 email 是「电子邮件」（第 01 个义项：通过网络发送的电子信件）；句意是列车到站前她查看了邮件。

pos.zh: 名词：电子邮件；电子邮件系统
及物动词：发电子邮件

derivatives.zh: 由 electronic mail 简化而来的基础词，义为「邮件」
带连字符的旧式拼写，义同 email
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「发邮件的人或邮件程序」

senses.title: A message sent over a network
senses.definition: a written message sent from one computer or phone to another through the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网从一台电脑或手机发送到另一台的书面信息
senses.example: She checked her email before the train arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 列车到站前她查看了邮件。
senses.why: The word joins electronic and mail, so an old paper letter keeps its name while its body turns into data travelling through wires.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 electronic 与 mail 合成，纸信的名字被保留下来，但信的内容变成了沿线路传输的数据。

senses.title: The email system
senses.definition: the whole system of accounts, servers and software used to send such messages
senses.definitionCN: 用来发送这类信息的账号、服务器与软件构成的整套系统
senses.example: The company moved all its email to the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把所有邮件系统都迁移到了云端。
senses.why: A single message and the network that carries it share one name, so email also means the postal system of the internet.
senses.whyCN: 单封邮件与承载它的网络共用一个名字，所以 email 也指互联网上的那套邮政系统。

senses.title: To send an email
senses.definition: to send a message to someone using email
senses.definitionCN: 用电子邮件给某人发送信息
senses.example: Please email me the draft by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前把草稿发邮件给我。
senses.why: Any mail noun in English can turn into a verb meaning to send it, so email follows mail and letter into action.
senses.whyCN: 英语里凡是「邮件」类名词都能转成表示「寄送」的动词，email 于是跟着 mail 一起从物品变成了动作。

intro.en: Email is a twentieth-century compound of electronic and mail, with mail itself coming from an old word for a bag.
intro.cn: email 是二十世纪由 electronic 与 mail 合成的词，而 mail 本身来自一个表示「袋子」的古老词。

items.en: Male meant a bag or bundle, especially a traveller's pack.
items.cn: 古法语 male 指袋子或包裹，尤指旅人的行囊。

items.en: English mail first meant a bag of letters, then the letters themselves.
items.cn: 中古英语 mail 先指一袋信件，后来指信件本身。

items.en: The postal sense became standard in Britain and America.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，邮政义在英美成为标准用法。

items.en: Computing coined electronic mail for messages passed between machines.
items.cn: 计算机领域造出 electronic mail，指机器之间传递的信息。

items.en: The clipped form email replaced the longer phrase and then became a verb.
items.cn: 缩略形式 email 取代了较长短语，随后又用作动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the mail family; the near-meaning group separates a message, a paper letter and the place where mail waits.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 mail 词族展开；近义组区分一条信息、一封纸质信与收件的地方。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels sent by post, or the system that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邮件、邮政」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: The older hyphenated spelling of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的旧式连字符拼写。

entries.definition: A box where mail is delivered or stored.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「信箱」，也可指电子邮箱。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, by any channel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消息」，可经任何渠道传递。

entries.definition: A written message on paper, usually posted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信件」，通常写在纸上邮寄。

entries.definition: The folder where incoming email is collected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收件箱」，是邮件到达后聚集的地方。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read email as electronic mail, then follow the letter into a message, a system and a verb.

normal.en: You can email a file or a person.

definition_zh: 使尴尬；使难堪；使为难；阻碍
definition_en: to make someone feel ashamed or awkward; to cause difficulty for someone or something
core_image: 被一道看不见的栏杆围住，进退都不自在
scene: 台上忽然忘词，他脸颊一下红到耳根。The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrass 是「使难堪」（第 01 个义项：让人感到羞愧不自在）；句意是长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。

pos.zh: 及物动词：使尴尬；使难堪；使为难

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「尴尬；难堪」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「感到尴尬的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「令人尴尬的」

senses.title: To make someone feel awkward
senses.definition: to make a person feel ashamed, nervous or socially uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到羞愧、紧张或在人前不自在
senses.example: The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。
senses.why: The old verb meant to block or entangle, so the core picture is being caught behind a barrier with no easy way out, which is exactly how social awkwardness feels.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词原本表示阻挡、缠住，核心画面是被栏杆困住、找不到出口，这正是社交尴尬的感受。

senses.title: To put someone in a difficult position
senses.definition: to cause problems or difficulties for a person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 给个人或机构造成麻烦与困难
senses.example: The question embarrassed the government.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题让政府很为难。
senses.why: Being blocked is not only social but practical, so the same verb describes a person or body trapped by an awkward problem.
senses.whyCN: 被挡住不只是社交上的事，也可能是实际处境，于是同一个动词也形容人或机构被难题困住。

senses.title: To hamper or obstruct, in older use
senses.definition: to hinder or obstruct movement or progress, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍移动或进展，这是较旧且罕见的义项
senses.example: Fallen trees embarrassed the advance of the column.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树木阻碍了队伍前进。
senses.why: The earliest sense is physical obstruction, and the social sense grew from it; the old meaning survives mainly in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思就是物理上的阻挡，社交义由此长出；旧义如今主要残留在正式书面语里。

intro.en: Embarrass came through French from a verb meaning to bar in, so its oldest picture is a barrier, not a blush.
intro.cn: embarrass 经法语来自一个意为「用栏杆围住」的动词，所以它最古老的画面是障碍，而不是脸红。

items.en: Imbarrare meant to bar in, built on barra, a bar.
items.cn: imbarrare 意为用栏杆围住，其根是 barra（栏杆）。

items.en: Embarrasser carried the sense of blocking or entangling.
items.cn: embarrasser 带有阻挡、缠住的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb first for physical hindrance.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，最初指物理上的阻碍。

items.en: The social sense of making someone uncomfortable became common.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，表示让人不自在的社交义变得常见。

items.en: Today the awkward sense dominates, while the obstructive sense is rare and formal.
items.cn: 今天尴尬义占主导，阻碍义则少见且正式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -ment, -ed and -ing family; the near-meaning group separates shame, humiliation and plain confusion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 -ment、-ed、-ing 词族展开；近义组区分羞愧、羞辱与单纯的困惑。

senses.title: The feeling of awkwardness
senses.definition: the uncomfortable feeling of being ashamed or self-conscious
senses.definitionCN: 因羞愧或在人前不自在而产生的不舒服感受
senses.example: A wave of embarrassment swept over the team.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵尴尬掠过整个团队。
senses.why: The noun names the state of being barred in, so embarrassment is the inner experience of having no easy social exit.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「被栏杆围住」的状态，所以 embarrassment 就是找不到社交出口时的内在体验。

senses.title: A person or thing that causes shame
senses.definition: someone or something that makes a group or person feel ashamed
senses.definitionCN: 让某个群体或个人感到羞耻的人或事物
senses.example: The failed launch was an embarrassment to the company.
senses.exampleCN: 发射失败让公司非常难堪。
senses.why: By a common shift, the cause of the feeling borrows the name of the feeling, so an embarrassing event becomes an embarrassment.
senses.whyCN: 常见的一种转喻是让「感受的原因」借用「感受」的名字，于是令人难堪的事件本身也叫 embarrassment。

senses.title: A difficult situation, often financial
senses.definition: a difficult or complicated situation, especially a financial one
senses.definitionCN: 困难复杂的处境，尤指经济上的拮据
senses.example: The family faced financial embarrassment after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这家人陷入经济困境。
senses.why: The old barrier sense survives as a general trap, so the noun can still mean being stuck in a difficult position.
senses.whyCN: 古老的栏杆义作为「被困住」保留下来，所以这个名词仍能表示陷在困难处境里。

senses.title: The office of an ambassador
senses.definition: the official building where an ambassador works and often lives

senses.example: She went to the embassy for a visa.
senses.exampleCN: 她去大使馆办签证。
senses.why: The word first named the office or mission of an ambassador, and the building that houses it took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指大使的职务与使命，后来承载这项职务的建筑也沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The staff of a diplomatic mission

senses.example: The embassy was evacuated during the storm.

definition_zh: 拥抱；欣然接受；包含；包围
definition_en: to hold someone closely in the arms; to accept an idea willingly; to include or contain
core_image: 两条手臂合拢，把一个人或一个念头整个圈进来
scene: 车站重逢，两人隔着人群张开手臂。They embraced at the station after two years apart.
sceneCN: 这里 embrace 是「拥抱」（第 01 个义项：用双臂抱紧某人）；句意是分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。

senses.title: To hold someone in the arms
senses.definition: to put your arms around someone and hold them closely
senses.definitionCN: 用双臂环住某人并抱紧
senses.example: They embraced at the station after two years apart.
senses.exampleCN: 分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。
senses.why: The French source joins in- with brace, an arm, so the word's body is literally putting arms around someone.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源把 in-（在内）与 brace（手臂）结合，所以这个词的身体动作字面就是「把手臂环上去」。

senses.title: To accept an idea willingly
senses.definition: to accept a belief, change or opportunity with enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 热情地接受某种观念、变化或机会
senses.example: The company embraced the new technology.
senses.exampleCN: 公司欣然接受了这项新技术。
senses.why: An idea can be taken into the arms the way a person is, so embracing a plan means drawing it close instead of pushing it away.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能像人一样被抱进怀里，所以 embrace a plan 就是把计划拉近，而不是推开。

senses.title: To include or contain
senses.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为更大整体的一部分包含进来
senses.example: The course embraces both theory and practice.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课兼顾理论与实践。
senses.why: Arms that close around a group enclose everything inside, so the verb extends from hugging a person to containing a range of things.
senses.whyCN: 手臂合拢会把一群东西都圈在里面，于是这个动词从抱人扩展到涵盖一系列事物。

intro.en: Embrace came from Old French, where the word for arm supplied the picture of arms closing around something.
intro.cn: embrace 来自古法语，其中表示「手臂」的词提供了双臂合拢的画面。

items.en: Bracchium meant the forearm or arm.
items.cn: bracchium 意为前臂或手臂。

items.en: Brace meant an arm, and the verb embracier meant to put arms around.
items.cn: brace 意为手臂，动词 embracier 意为用双臂环抱。

items.en: English borrowed embrace in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 embrace。

items.en: The figurative sense of accepting an idea appeared.
items.cn: 表示接受某种观念的比喻义出现。

items.en: The verb now covers hugging, accepting and including.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个动词涵盖拥抱、接受与包含。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the arm root; the near-meaning group separates a hug, acceptance and inclusion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「手臂」词根展开；近义组区分拥抱、接受与包含。

entries.definition: An ornament worn around the wrist, from the arm root.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「手链」，词根仍是「手臂」。

entries.definition: A support or pair, from the same Old French arm word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「支架、一对」，源自古法语的手臂词。

entries.definition: The act of embracing, a rare noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「拥抱、接受」，较少见。

entries.definition: To hold someone closely, the plain everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥抱」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To agree to take something offered.

entries.definition: To have something as part of a whole.

normal.en: Em- plus brace, an arm: put arms around.

normal.en: To embrace change is to hold it close.

normal.en: A course that embraces theory and practice contains both.

abstract.en: Embrace is a hug that learned to hold ideas.

branches.cn: 身与心：同一个动作既欢迎人，也欢迎想法。

definition_zh: 出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出
definition_en: to come out from a hidden place; to become known; to come into existence; to survive a difficult period
core_image: 水面下的一团影子慢慢升起，终于露出水面
scene: 云层裂开，太阳从背后露出边缘。The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 emerge 是「露出、出现」（第 01 个义项：从遮蔽处出来）；句意是太阳从云层后露出。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「出现；兴起」
由动词加 -ent 构成，义为「新兴的；浮现的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「新兴的；正在出现的」

senses.title: To come out from a hidden place
senses.definition: to move out of water, darkness or another covering and become visible
senses.definitionCN: 从水中、暗处或其他遮盖物里出来并变得可见
senses.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从云层后露出。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mergere, to dip or sink, so the core picture is something rising out of the water into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mergere（浸入、下沉）组合，核心画面就是某物从水里升起、露出水面。

senses.title: To become known
senses.definition: to become known or apparent after being hidden or unclear
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏或不清晰的事情变得为人所知
senses.example: New facts emerged during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。
senses.why: Facts can rise out of obscurity just as an object rises out of water, so the physical surfacing becomes a metaphor for disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 事实能像物体升出水面一样从模糊中浮现，于是这个物理动作变成了「真相显露」的比喻。

senses.title: To come into existence
senses.definition: to begin to exist or become established
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在或逐渐确立
senses.example: A new industry emerged in the coastal city.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新兴产业在这座沿海城市兴起。
senses.why: What rises into view did not exist for the observer before, so emergence also names the birth of a thing or trend.
senses.whyCN: 对观察者来说，升起并进入视野的东西此前并不存在，所以 emergence 也用来命名事物或趋势的诞生。

senses.title: To survive a difficult period
senses.definition: to come out of a difficult experience in a new or stronger position
senses.definitionCN: 从艰难经历中走出来，处于新的或更强的位置
senses.example: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。
senses.why: Coming out of water is also coming out of danger, so the verb describes a person or group that survives a trial and steps into the open.
senses.whyCN: 从水里出来也意味着从危险中出来，所以这个动词形容人或群体熬过考验、走到开阔处。

intro.en: Emerge comes straight from Latin emergere, to rise out of a liquid.
intro.cn: emerge 直接来自拉丁语 emergere，意为从液体中升起。

items.en: Mergere meant to dip, plunge or sink.
items.cn: mergere 意为浸入、扎入或下沉。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to rise out of water.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为从水中升起。

items.en: The participle described something coming up into view.
items.cn: 其分词形容某物升上来、进入视野。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for physical surfacing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，表示物理上的浮出。

items.en: The sense widened to facts becoming known and new things coming into being.
items.cn: 词义扩大到事实显露与新事物产生。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the merge root and its derived nouns; the near-meaning group separates appearing, surfacing and arising.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 merge 词根及其派生名词展开；近义组区分出现、浮出水面与产生。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现、兴起」的过程。

entries.definition: Newly appearing or developing.

entries.definition: To sink into or combine, from the same Latin verb without e-.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「合并、融入」，同一个拉丁动词去掉 e- 前缀。

entries.definition: To become visible, often without effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现」，常不带努力感。

entries.definition: To come up to the top, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浮出水面」，可实指也可比喻。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of problems or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生」，多用于问题或局面。

normal.en: A new market can emerge overnight.
normal.cn: 新市场可以在一夜之间兴起。

normal.en: A team can emerge stronger from a crisis.
normal.cn: 一个团队能从危机中变得更强。

abstract.en: Emerge is a birth told as a surfacing.

senses.title: To send out light, heat or sound
senses.definition: to send out energy such as light, heat, sound or radiation

senses.example: The old stove emitted a steady wave of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 旧炉子持续散发热浪。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mittere, to send, so emit is literally to send something outward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mittere（发送）组合，所以 emit 字面就是「往外送」。

senses.title: To send out gas or waste
senses.definition: to release gas, smoke or other waste into the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把气体、烟雾或其他废物释放到环境中
senses.example: The factory emits less smoke than before.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂排放的烟比以前少。
senses.why: The same outward sending applies to unwanted substances, so the verb became the standard word for pollution sources.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「往外送」也适用于不想要的物质，于是这个动词成了描述污染源的标准词。

senses.title: To utter or express
senses.definition: to say or express something, especially a sound or opinion

senses.example: She emitted a sigh of relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她松了一口气。
senses.why: A voice sends sound outward as a lamp sends light, so the verb extends from physical energy to human utterance.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音把声音送出去，就像灯把光送出去，于是这个动词从物理能量延伸到人的言语。

senses.title: A strong feeling

senses.title: Relating to emotions
senses.definition: connected with feelings rather than with pure reason
senses.definitionCN: 与感受有关，而不是与纯粹理性有关
senses.example: Children need emotional support as well as food.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子除了食物，也需要情感支持。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds -al to emotion, so it labels whatever belongs to the stirred inner life.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在 emotion 后加 -al，用来标记属于「被搅动的内心生活」的一切。

senses.title: Easily moved to strong feeling
senses.definition: showing feelings openly or becoming upset easily
senses.definitionCN: 公开表露感受，或很容易被触动
senses.example: He became emotional when he spoke about his mother.
senses.exampleCN: 谈到母亲时他动情了。
senses.why: A person whose inner water is easily stirred is called emotional, so the adjective also describes a low threshold for feeling.
senses.whyCN: 内心水面容易被搅动的人就被称为 emotional，所以这个形容词也形容感受的门槛很低。

senses.title: Causing strong feelings
senses.definition: producing strong feelings in an audience or reader
senses.definitionCN: 在观众或读者心中激起强烈感受
senses.example: The final scene was deeply emotional.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一场戏非常动人。
senses.why: A scene can stir the viewer the way a hand stirs water, so the adjective turns from the feeler to the thing that makes others feel.
senses.whyCN: 一场戏能像手搅水一样搅动观众，于是这个形容词从「感受者」转向「让别人产生感受的事物」。

intro.en: Emotional is a native English formation from emotion plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: emotional 是英语在 emotion 后加形容词词尾 -al 构成的本土派生词。

items.en: The ultimate verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 最终源头动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective emotional was formed with -al.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，加 -al 构成形容词 emotional。

items.en: It now covers the emotional life, a person's temperament and moving works of art.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖情感生活、人的性情与动人的艺术作品。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates sentimental, moving and passionate.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分多愁善感、动人以及充满激情。

senses.title: In terms of emotions
senses.definition: in a way that concerns a person's feelings or emotional needs
senses.definitionCN: 在涉及一个人的感受或情感需求的方面
senses.example: The children were emotionally neglected.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子在情感上被忽视了。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to emotional, so it marks the emotional dimension of a situation rather than its physical side.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 emotional 加 -ly 构成，所以它标记的是一件事的情感维度，而不是物理层面。

senses.title: With strong feeling
senses.definition: in a manner showing strong or barely controlled feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈或难以控制的感情的方式
senses.example: She spoke emotionally about the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 她谈到失去时动了情。
senses.why: When the inner pond is stirred, speech itself can shake, so the adverb describes an action carried out with visible feeling.
senses.whyCN: 内心的水面被搅动时，连说话都会发抖，所以这个副词形容一个带着明显感情完成的动作。

senses.title: In an easily affected state
senses.definition: in a state where feelings are easily aroused or hard to manage
senses.definitionCN: 处于感情容易被激起或难以控制的状态
senses.example: He reacted emotionally to the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他对批评的反应很情绪化。
senses.why: A person whose feelings rise quickly acts from that rising rather than from calm thought, so the adverb can also signal a low emotional threshold.
senses.whyCN: 感受升得快的人会顺着这股上升行动，而不是按冷静思考行动，所以这个副词也能暗示情感门槛很低。

senses.title: The ruler of an empire
senses.definition: the male sovereign who rules an empire
senses.definitionCN: 统治一个帝国的男性君主
senses.example: The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
senses.exampleCN: 皇帝在大殿接见使节。
senses.why: The Latin source is a commander who gives orders, so the emperor is the one whose command holds an empire together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是发号施令的统帅，所以皇帝就是那个用命令把帝国维系在一起的人。

senses.title: A monarch with this title
senses.definition: a king or sovereign who formally holds the title of emperor
senses.definitionCN: 正式拥有皇帝称号的国王或君主
senses.example: The emperor of Japan has a largely ceremonial role.
senses.exampleCN: 日本天皇的角色主要是礼仪性的。
senses.why: A title can outlive the power behind it, so emperor also names a rank that may now be ceremonial.
senses.whyCN: 称号可以比它背后的权力活得更久，所以 emperor 也指一种如今可能只剩礼仪意义的位号。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: a person who dominates a particular activity or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在某一活动或行业中占据统治地位的人
senses.example: He was called the emperor of modern retail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被称为现代零售业的皇帝。
senses.why: One who rules a territory and one who rules a market share the image of command, so the title extends to industry leaders.
senses.whyCN: 统治疆域的人与统治市场份额的人共享「发号施令」的画面，于是这个称号扩展到行业领袖身上。

intro.en: Emperor goes back to Latin imperator, a commander, and to the verb imperare, to command.

senses.title: Special importance
senses.definition: special importance or attention given to something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某事物的特别重要性或关注
senses.example: The teacher placed emphasis on the main verb.
senses.exampleCN: 老师强调了主要动词。
senses.why: The Greek source means a showing forth, so emphasis is the act of making one thing stand out from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头意为「显现出来」，所以 emphasis 就是让某一样东西从其余部分中凸显出来的动作。

senses.title: Stress on a word or syllable
senses.definition: extra force given to a word or syllable when speaking
senses.definitionCN: 说话时给某个词或音节额外的力度
senses.example: He said the word with emphasis.
senses.exampleCN: 他加重语气说了那个词。
senses.why: Speaking makes one sound stand out by force, which is the same showing forth applied to the voice.
senses.whyCN: 说话时用力度让某个声音凸显出来，这就是「显现」用在嗓音上的版本。

senses.title: Force of expression
senses.definition: the strength or prominence of a statement, design or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 陈述、设计或姿态所具有的力度与醒目程度
senses.example: The dark frame gives emphasis to the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 深色画框让这幅画更突出。
senses.why: Anything that makes a feature stand out, whether words, color or shape, carries emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能让某个特征凸显出来的东西，无论是文字、颜色还是形状，都带有 emphasis。

intro.en: Emphasis came into English from Latin, which borrowed it from Greek, where it meant a showing forth.
intro.cn: emphasis 经拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语又借自希腊语，原意为「显现出来」。

items.en: Phainein meant to show or bring to light.
items.cn: phainein 意为显示、使显现。

items.en: Emphasis meant an appearance or a meaning shown forth.
items.cn: emphasis 意为显现、显露出来的意义。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun unchanged in meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊名词，意义不变。

items.en: English emphasis first named force of expression.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，最初指表达的力度。

items.en: It now covers importance, vocal stress and visual prominence.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖重要性、语音重音与视觉突出。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emphasis family; the near-meaning group separates stress, accent and importance.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emphasis 词族展开；近义组区分重音、口音与重要性。

senses.definitionCN: 说明或表明某事特别重要
senses.example: The report emphasizes the need for care.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调需要谨慎。
senses.why: The verb is emphasis turned into action, so to emphasize is to make one point show forth from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是 emphasis 变成动作，所以 emphasize 就是让某一个要点从其余部分中显现出来。

senses.title: To stress a word in speech
senses.definition: to say a word or syllable with extra force
senses.definitionCN: 用额外的力度说出某个词或音节
senses.example: She emphasized the word never.
senses.exampleCN: 她重读了「绝不」这个词。
senses.why: Voice can do what a spotlight does, so the verb also names the act of striking one syllable harder.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音也能做聚光灯做的事，所以这个动词也指把某个音节读得更重。

senses.title: To make something visually prominent
senses.definition: to make a feature more noticeable in a design or image

senses.example: The designer emphasized the logo with a bright border.

senses.why: If importance can be shown by voice, it can also be shown by color and line, so the verb reaches visual design.
senses.whyCN: 如果重要性可以用声音表现，也就能用颜色与线条表现，于是这个动词延伸到视觉设计。

definition_en: a group of countries ruled by one sovereign; the territory so ruled; a large business group
core_image: 一张地图被同一条边界从海岸连到山脉
scene: 地图上一块块颜色被同一条边界连起来，向远方延伸。The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 empire 是「帝国疆域」（第 01 个义项：由一个君主统治的多个地区）；句意是这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。

senses.title: A group of lands under one ruler
senses.definition: a group of countries or peoples ruled by a single sovereign
senses.definitionCN: 由一个君主统治的一组国家或民族
senses.example: The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。
senses.why: The Latin source means command, so an empire is the whole territory where one command is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「命令」，所以帝国就是整套「同一条命令被服从」的疆域。

senses.title: The territory itself
senses.definition: the land and peoples considered as one domain
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一个整体的土地与人民
senses.example: Trade routes crossed the empire in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 商路四通八达地穿过帝国疆域。
senses.why: Command and the land that receives it are named together, so empire also means the map rather than the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 命令与接受命令的土地被一起命名，所以 empire 也指那张地图，而不是统治者本人。

senses.title: A large business group
senses.definition: a very large group of companies controlled by one person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人或组织控制的庞大公司群
senses.example: He built a media empire from a single newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他从一家报纸起家，打造了一个媒体帝国。
senses.why: A market can be ruled like a territory, so the word for political command extends to commercial dominance.
senses.whyCN: 市场可以像疆域一样被统治，于是这个表示政治统治的词扩展到了商业版图。

senses.title: Supreme authority, in older use
senses.definition: supreme command or dominion, an older abstract sense
senses.definitionCN: 最高的统治权或支配权，是较旧的抽象义项
senses.example: The old chronicle speaks of the empire of reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史谈到理性的统治。
senses.why: Before it named a place, imperium named the power itself, and empire can still mean dominion in formal or literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 在指一片土地之前，imperium 指的是权力本身，所以 empire 在正式或文学语境中仍可表示支配权。

intro.cn: empire 是经法语借入的拉丁语词，其词尾属于历史沉积而非能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: Imperare, imperium and imperator are recorded Latin forms of command and rule.
latinIntro.cn: imperare、imperium 与 imperator 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，表示命令与统治。
